mode: Reused existing generated photo and presentation sources; composed one fixed embedded font separately with size-only changes. No new image generation or new font preparation.
fontLicensePolicy: The existing renamed Source Sans 3 Regular illustration instance is reused unchanged with original source and OFL notice retained. Optical sizing is disabled and the exact same static font file and weight400 are used throughout.

roleScales.units: artwork layout units, not physical points or recommended CSS sizes

comparisonPolicy: Programme: eleven size values change to consolidate eight distinct values into four roles. Review: title31 to40 and section headings30/29 to28; body22/meta20 untouched. Phone: title52 to36 and section30 to24, with body22/meta20 untouched. No variable other than declared font-size attributes changes inside the artifacts. Copy, fixed line breaks, fonts, optical cut, requested weights, anchors, baselines, alignment, colors, photo bytes/crops, paper/device and lighting are identical.

verification.textBounds: within the declared paper or phone surface
verification.pixelCheck: Only intended declared type-scale intervention regions differ.
verification.scope: All six saved desktop/stacked PNGs visually inspected. The one embedded font loads and full-size SVG img rendering equals inline rendering byte for byte. Browser pixel checks find no changes outside declared text regions. Copy fits the paper/phone surfaces and narrow views have no horizontal overflow. Exact DOM checks allow only declared font-size attributes and preserve copy, anchors, baselines, line breaks, weights, font/optical design, all image bytes/crops and non-text geometry. Semantic checks validate role sizes, eight-to-four consolidation, the shared print scale and unchanged phone body/metadata. Article-renderer markup is checked separately.

limitations: No audience study, numerical performance benefit, physical proof, implemented responsive booking behavior, complete accessibility evaluation or production-route result. Frozen anchors isolate size selection and do not demonstrate reflow or content moving upward. Original examples may be appropriate for equal-status panels or promotional use. Ratios and chosen values are editorial choices, not a universally optimal scale.
